avoid_supplements.name: High-dose vitamin C (>2000 mg/day)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May increase urinary pH and oseltamivir renal clearance, potentially reducing antiviral efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Limit vitamin C supplementation to RDA levels (75-90 mg/day) during oseltamivir therapy

caution_supplements.name: Probiotics
caution_supplements.mechanism: Oseltamivir may reduce beneficial gut flora; probiotics may help maintain GI microbiota
caution_supplements.action: May use concurrently but separate administration by 2+ hours if GI upset occurs

caution_supplements.name: Ginger supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have mild antiemetic properties to counter oseltamivir-induced nausea
caution_supplements.action: Safe to use; may provide symptomatic relief for GI side effects

caution_foods.name: High-fat meals
caution_foods.mechanism: May delay oseltamivir absorption and peak plasma concentration
caution_foods.action: Administer oseltamivir with food to reduce nausea, but high-fat meals may be suboptimal for absorption timing

caution_foods.name: Dairy products
caution_foods.mechanism: Calcium may minimally chelate oseltamivir; separate administration recommended
caution_foods.action: Take oseltamivir 1-2 hours before or after dairy-heavy meals if possible

monitoring_notes: Oseltamivir undergoes minimal hepatic metabolism and is primarily renin-cleared; interactions are uncommon. Monitor renal function in patients with compromised kidney function, as oseltamivir accumulation may increase neuropsychiatric side effects.
